newsitem.title: USA: NYC gets top funds in school construction bill.
newsitem.headline: NYC gets top funds in school construction bill.

text.p: New York City, a Chicago school district and Los Angeles Unified school district would get top federal dollars under the local funding portion of President Clinton's school construction bill proposed on Friday, the U.S. Education Department said.
The White House sent Congress legislation that would provide $5 billion over four years to help states and localities rebuild America's crumbling schools.

Roughly $2.45 billion of the total $5 billion pot would cover direct grants to the 100 school districts nationwide, with the greatest number of poor children (based on General Accounting Office figures).

The following would be the 20 largest recipients of local grants: New York City, 287.3 million; City of Chicago School District 29, $117.1 million; Los Angeles Unified school district, $115.7 million; Detroit City School District, $72.7 million; Philadelphia City School District, $63.2 million; Dade County (Florida) School District, $50 million; Houston ISD, $37.7 million; Wilwaukee School District, $34.1 million; Baltimore City, Md. Public School System, $31.4 million; Cleveland City School District, $26.6 million; Dallas Independent School District, $25 million; Orleans Parish School Board in Louisiana, $24.5 million; Memphis City School District in Tennessee, $20.8 million; Boston School District, $17 million; Newark City, N.J., $16.8 million; San Antonio ISD in Texas, $16.6 million; Broward County School District in Florida, $16.4 million; Buffalo City Schools in New York, $16.2 million; San Diego City Unified in California, $16.1 million; and Hillsborough County School District in Florida, $15.8 million.
